table:identity_associations.note: Pairs a row's local id with the id Conductor's server gave it (main @587576). D103 names it as not built: our cloud rows keep the id the Mac gave them.

table:symlinks_pending_deletion.item: Table symlinks_pending_deletion; its purpose is unknown, maybe deleting worktrees that contain symlinks.

table:session_messages_outbox.note: Follow-up messages waiting to be sent, with their order, state and last error (main @1209573, "This queued message could not be read"). Ours is queued_messages (CHAT-04).

table:session_pending_messages_state.note: In Conductor's cache.db: the pause state and generation of a server-hosted session's pending messages (main @1213029). Our cloud chats keep the pause in sessions (D103).

table:session_pending_messages.note: In Conductor's cache.db: the pending messages of a session its server hosts, with sender, revision and generation from Roundhouse (main @1213218, keyed session-pending-messages:). Our cloud chats queue in queued_messages like local ones (D103).

table:session_assets_outbox.note: The attachments of queued follow-ups (main @1216310). Ours keeps a queued message's attachments in queued_messages.attachment_paths.

table:client_cache_session_state.note: The cache version of a cloud session copied from Roundhouse (main @1403143). D103 keeps a cloud chat's events in session_events and names this table as not built.

table:session_messages.note: Conductor's old message table, written beside session_events. D006 keeps session_events as the only chat history.

table:client_cache_session_segments.note: Which feed segments of a cloud session Conductor has loaded from Roundhouse (main @1403375). D103 keeps a cloud chat's events in session_events, so there is no segment cache; it names this table as not built.

table:session_state.note: A chat's last live state and config. Ours keeps the live state in session_live_state and the config in sessions.config.

table:session_messages_outbox_state.note: When a chat's follow-up queue was paused (paused_at). Ours keeps it in sessions.queue_paused_at.

table:terminal_sessions.note: A terminal's row, with what a restore needs. Ours is terminals; its screen_state keeps the screen modes (alternate screen, bracketed paste) the PTY's snapshot reports (pty.rs, PLAT-08).

table:navigation_sections.note: The sidebar's sections, scoped by Conductor's server, organisation and user. Ours keeps them in sections for this Mac (NAV-04).

table:navigation_section_memberships.note: Which workspace sits in which sidebar section. Ours is section_members (NAV-04).

table:_sqlx_migrations.note: sqlx's migration ledger: Conductor's SQL plugin keeps it, and so does our shell's migrator (D137).

table:identity_acceptances.note: A table Conductor's schema creates that no frontend or sidecar statement names (only conductor-schema.sql has it).

table:local_workspace_deletion_tombstone.note: Read only by the phone relay host, which tells a paired phone which local workspaces were deleted (sidecar.js @1610290).

table:local_workspace_revision_counter.note: Read only by the phone relay host, which lists the local workspaces changed since a revision for a paired phone (sidecar.js @1610003, used by the relay at @1623129).

table:migration_rollbacks.note: Each Conductor migration registers its undo SQL here, for a repository script that moves a database down (native-and-sidecar-map A11). Ours has no down-migrations: a database newer than the app asks the user to update (db.rs, PLAT-17).
